title: Lesson 9: Living the Fruit of the Spirit
description: Jesus is the vine, the Father is the vinedresser, and you are a branch. Sanctification is the Spirit's lifelong work of making you more like Jesus, and the fruit of Galatians 5:22-23, one fruit with nine expressions, is the evidence. You do not manufacture this fruit. You abide in Jesus, and His Spirit grows it.

blocks.text: In the last lesson you saw what Jesus accomplished for you at the cross: grace, mercy, justified, righteous. Every debt paid. Now a question follows naturally: if all of that is truly done, why do I still struggle? Why does my anger still flare up, or my fear still win, or my kindness still run dry? That is not a crisis of faith. That is sanctification.

Sanctification is the ongoing work of the Holy Spirit to make you more and more like Jesus. You were justified in a moment. You are being sanctified over a lifetime. On the last night before the cross, Jesus gave His friends a picture of how that growth happens.

blocks.title: The Vine and the Branches
blocks.text:
It was the night before the cross. Jesus had washed His disciples' feet, shared the bread and the cup, and told them He was going away. Their hearts were troubled. So He gave them a picture they could carry, taken from the vineyards on the hills all around them.

"I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser. Every branch in me that does not bear fruit he takes away, and every branch that does bear fruit he prunes, that it may bear more fruit. Already you are clean because of the word that I have spoken to you. Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit by itself, unless it abides in the vine, neither can you, unless you abide in me. I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever abides in me and I in him, he it is that bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing." (John 15:1-5)

A branch never strains to make grapes. It does not clench its jaw or try harder. It simply stays joined to the vine, and the life of the vine flows into it until the fruit comes. Cut it off, and it withers. Leave it connected, and it bears fruit season after season.

Notice who is who. Jesus is the vine. All the life comes from Him. The Father is the vinedresser. He tends, protects, and prunes. You are a branch. Your job is not to produce. It is to abide: to stay, to remain, to keep living where you already are.

And before Jesus gives a single command, He says, "Already you are clean." You did not graft yourself into the vine. Grace put you there. Abiding is simply staying where grace has put you. That same night Jesus promised to send the Holy Spirit to be with you forever (John 14:16-17), and the Spirit is how the life of the Vine flows into the branches. That is why Paul calls it the fruit of the Spirit.
Here is the one thing to carry out of this lesson: you do not manufacture the fruit. You abide in Jesus, and His Spirit grows it in you.
One Fruit, Nine Expressions
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law.

Notice Paul does not say fruits of the Spirit, as if each one is a separate crop. He says fruit, singular. All nine belong together, like the segments of a single orange. You cannot have the Spirit living in you and only pick the slices you like. Where the branch stays in the Vine, the whole fruit grows. Walk through the nine below.

In your heart. Love comes first because everything else grows from it. It is not a feeling you fall into but a commitment to another's good, rooted in how God has already loved you. Joy is not happiness that rises and falls with your circumstances. It is the delight of the man who found treasure in a field and "in his joy" sold everything to buy it (Matthew 13:44). Peace is not the absence of the storm but the presence of the One who stood up in the boat and said, "Peace! Be still!" (Mark 4:39). He is already in the boat with you.

In your relationships. Patience is active trust, slow to anger with people and steady when life runs off your plan. Kindness is God's own tenderness toward the undeserving, reproduced in you. Micah 6:8 does not only tell you to act kind. It tells you to "love kindness." Goodness is a Spirit-grown desire to do good. You were not saved by good works, but you were saved for them (Ephesians 2:10).

In your character. Faithfulness keeps its word when it is inconvenient and keeps showing up when you would rather disappear. Gentleness is strength under control. Jesus had the power to judge every person in the room, and He knelt to wash their feet instead, even Judas's. Self-control is not restriction for its own sake. It is the freedom of not being mastered by your appetites, so you can love God and others well.
9.1 - Which expression of the fruit feels least grown in you right now?
9.2 - Think of a relationship in your life that is difficult right now. Which fruit do you most need the Spirit to grow in you for that person?
We Fight Because We Have One

Here is the most important thing to hold onto: the fruit of the Spirit is not an achievement you manufacture. It is the evidence of something God is already doing. We are not fighting to have a relationship with God. We are fighting because we have one. Sanctification is not you trying to become holy enough to deserve His presence. It is His Spirit, already living in you, growing what He planted when you first believed.
Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling, for it is God who works in you, both to will and to work for his good pleasure.

Both things are true at the same time. God works in you, and you work it out. He is not passive, and you are not passive. But here is the order: His work makes your work possible. A branch is not lazy. It stays joined, it drinks, it grows. But it never forgets where its life comes from.
9.3 - Do you tend to strain to grow on your own strength, or to wait for God to change you without doing your part?
The Vinedresser's Pruning

The wild vine sprawling over a fence looks free. It grows where it wants and produces small, sour grapes. The pruned vine on the trellis submits to painful cuts and bears fruit that is sweet, abundant, and worth sharing. Remember who holds the shears. The Father is the vinedresser, and you are the branch. He prunes the branches that already bear fruit, "that it may bear more fruit" (John 15:2). The pruning is not punishment. It is preparation. The cuts make room for a better harvest.
9.4 - Is there an area of your life that feels like pruning right now? How might God be using it to prepare you for more fruit?
This Week's Practice

Each morning this week, read John 15:4-5 slowly. Name the one fruit you wrote down in 9.1, and pray one honest sentence: "Jesus, I cannot grow this on my own. I will stay close to You today." Each evening, take two minutes to look back. Where did you see that fruit show up? Where did you run on your own strength? Thank Him for the first. Confess the second, and rest in His word: you are already clean. Do not grade the harvest. Just stay connected.
Lesson 9 Review

Jesus is the vine, the Father is the vinedresser, and you are a branch. You do not manufacture the fruit. You abide in Jesus, and His Spirit grows it in you: one fruit with nine expressions. Fruit takes time. A tree can stand in a backyard looking ordinary for a whole year before one fall morning its branches hang heavy with fruit. The fruit of the Spirit does not save you. Faith in Jesus does that. But the fruit shows you and the watching world that the Vine is real and that something is growing.
In the next lesson, you will learn what to do when you drift away from the Vine, because you will. And the Father already knows how to bring you home.
